newsitem.title: EGYPT: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon rates Commercial International Bank/CIB "strong buy".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Salomon rates Commercial International Bank/CIB "strong buy".

text.p: Salomon Brothers gave a "strong buy" recommendation to Egypt's Commercial International Bank/CIB in an equity research report available in Cairo on Wednesday.
"Excellent management with a proactive expansion strategy and an ideal growth platform should result in 22 percent compound asset growth over the next decade," it said.
"We believe that the combination of high volume growth with fairly stable adjusted ROE (return on equity) allows us to set a price target for the shares at around 92 pounds," it added.
Salomon Brothers wrote the report when the share price was 70.25 pounds ($20.70). On Wednesday the shares traded at between 71.00 and 72.40 pounds on the Egyptian stock exchange.
The report predicted that CIB's net income in calendar 1997, the bank's financial year, would rise to 270.99 million pounds, from 241.26 million in 1996.
It would then rise to 311.42 million in 1998 and 368.10 million in 1999, it forecast. There are 50 million shares.
The bank was the first Egyptian company to float its shares in London in the form of global depositary receipts (GDRs).
